title: Rainwater Droplet Screen Refraction Simulation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive Three.js rainwater droplet screen refraction simulation. The scene simulates looking through a rain-covered glass window at a 3D scene behind it, with physically-based droplet refraction distortion applied as a post-processing effect.

ASSET LOADING:
- Load 'DamagedHelmet.glb' using THREE.GLTFLoader from a CDN (e.g., unpkg or jsdelivr for Three.js r158+). Place the helmet at the origin, scaled to fill the view nicely (scale ~2.0). Add the helmet to the scene. Use OrbitControls for camera interaction on the underlying scene.

SCENE SETUP:
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera, FOV 50, positioned at (0, 0, 4), looking at origin.
- Lighting: One directional light (intensity 1.5, position 3,5,3), one ambient light (intensity 0.4), and one point light (intensity 1.0, position -2,-1,3) for dramatic helmet illumination.
- Background: Set a dark gradient or solid color (0x111122) so the helmet is the focal object.
- Renderer: Use WebGLRenderer with antialias, toneMapping set to ACESFilmicToneMapping, outputColorSpace sRGB.

RAINDROP SIMULATION SYSTEM:
- Maintain an array of raindrop objects. Each droplet has: {x, y, radius, speed, opacity, trail, age, active}.
- x,y are in normalized screen coordinates [0,1]. radius ranges [0.01, 0.06]. speed ranges [0.0005, 0.003] per frame. opacity [0.3, 1.0]. trail is an array of previous y positions (max 8 entries). age increments each frame.
- Start with 60 active droplets randomly distributed. Droplets fall downward (y increases). When a droplet's y > 1.1, it respawns at y ~ -0.1 with new random x and radius.
- Every 120 frames, spawn a 'burst' of 10 additional droplets at random positions to simulate gusts.

POST-PROCESSING REFRACTION SHADER:
- Render the 3D scene (helmet + lights) to an offscreen RenderTarget (same resolution as canvas).
- Use a fullscreen quad with a custom ShaderMaterial for the final output.
- The fragment shader samples the offscreen texture. For each fragment, iterate over all active droplets. If the fragment is within a droplet's radius, apply a UV offset (refraction distortion) proportional to the distance from the droplet center, simulating a lens effect. Use a cubic falloff: distortion = (1.0 - (dist/radius)^2)^2 * refractionStrength.
- refractionStrength is a uniform, default 0.03.
- Also render a subtle droplet highlight (specular glint) on each droplet: a small bright spot offset toward upper-left of each droplet to simulate light reflection on water.
- Apply a slight blur/chromatic aberration inside droplets: offset R, G, B channels by slightly different amounts.

TRAIL RENDERING:
- Each droplet leaves a wet trail behind it. In the shader, for each trail point, apply a smaller, fading refraction distortion (50% strength, 60% radius of the main droplet, opacity decreasing with trail index).

INTERACTIVE CONTROLS:
- Keyboard 'R': Toggle rain on/off. When off, no new droplets spawn, existing ones freeze in place.
- Keyboard 'ArrowUp': Increase refractionStrength by 0.005 (max 0.08).
- Keyboard 'ArrowDown': Decrease refractionStrength by 0.005 (min 0.005).
- Keyboard 'B': Toggle burst mode — when enabled, spawn 10 droplets every 60 frames instead of 120.
- Mouse click on canvas: Spawn a 'splash' of 8 droplets at the clicked normalized position, each with random velocity vectors radiating outward, radius [0.015, 0.04].
- DOM button '#clearBtn' (text 'Clear Drops'): Remove all active droplets instantly, reset count to 0. Rain will repopulate if rain is on.
- DOM button '#toggleTrailBtn' (text 'Toggle Trails'): Enable/disable trail rendering (trails still computed but shader skips them).

HUD OVERLAY:
- A semi-transparent HUD panel (top-left, dark background, white text, id='hud').
- Display: droplet count, refractionStrength (3 decimal places), rain status (ON/OFF), burst mode (ON/OFF), trails (ON/OFF), FPS.

STATE MANAGEMENT — window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
- dropletCount: number of active droplets
- refractionStrength: current refraction strength (number)
- rainActive: boolean, whether rain is running
- burstMode: boolean
- trailsEnabled: boolean
- fps: current FPS (number)
- frameCount: total frames rendered
- helmetLoaded: boolean, true once GLTF is loaded
- lastSplashTime: timestamp (ms) of last mouse-click splash, or 0
- splashCount: total number of splash events triggered
- dropletsSpawnedTotal: cumulative count of all droplets ever spawned
- renderTargetWidth: width of the offscreen render target
- renderTargetHeight: height of the offscreen render target
- dropletRadiusAvg: average radius of all active droplets (number)
- maxDropletAge: the age of the oldest active droplet

Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop. Ensure all values are always defined (never undefined or NaN).
physics_constraints: Droplets must fall downward with constant speed per droplet. Refraction distortion must use cubic falloff from droplet center. Droplet count must be conserved (spawned = active + recycled). No NaN values in any state field. Refraction strength must stay clamped [0.005, 0.08]. Splash droplets must radiate outward from click point. Trail length must not exceed 8 entries per droplet.
